quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards! They can also hover in place by flapping their wings up to 80 times per second. These tiny acrobats have exceptional memories and can remember every flower they've visited and how long it takes each one to refill with nectar.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Harbor Seals in Puget Sound
short_read.teaser: Harbor seals are year-round residents of the Strait of Juan de Fuca, and they're more social and playful than you might think. Learn about their daily routines, favorite resting spots, and how to spot them from shore.

medium_read.title: Hungarian Folk Art: The Language of Embroidery
medium_read.teaser: Traditional Hungarian embroidery tells stories through symbols and colors that have been passed down for centuries. Each region of Hungary developed its own distinctive patterns, creating a beautiful tapestry of cultural expression.

long_read.title: The Magnificent Rain Forests of Olympic National Park
long_read.teaser: Just south of Port Angeles, some of the most enchanting temperate rain forests in the world thrive with moss-draped trees and lush ferns. This journey explores the unique ecosystem where Roosevelt elk roam and ancient trees tell thousand-year-old stories.

port_angeles.title: Butterfly Season at Hurricane Ridge
port_angeles.description: August is peak butterfly season at Hurricane Ridge! On sunny days, you can spot dozens of species including the beautiful Olympic Marble butterfly, found only in the Olympic Mountains. The alpine meadows are alive with color as butterflies dance among the wildflowers.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats approximately ___ times per minute during flight.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Amazing! Yes, 1,200 beats per minute — that's about 20 times faster than a human heart at rest!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute when flying — an incredible pace!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: A hummingbird's heart actually beats about 1,200 times per minute during flight — that's faster than any other bird!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Despite their tiny size, hummingbirds have the highest metabolism of any animal on Earth. To fuel this incredible energy, they must eat half their body weight in sugar every day.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'hello' or 'goodbye'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Szia! That's right! It's a casual, friendly greeting you can use for both hello and goodbye.
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is 'Szia' (pronounced SEE-ah) — it's a warm, casual way to say both hello and goodbye to friends.
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is a unique language that's part of the Finno-Ugric family, making it quite different from neighboring European languages. It has 14 vowel sounds and uses extensive suffixes to modify word meanings.

puzzle_3.question: What type of tree is most common in Olympic National Park's rain forests?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Wonderful! Sitka Spruce trees dominate the rain forests, growing up to 300 feet tall and living for 700 years. They love the moist, mild climate near the coast!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: The answer is Sitka Spruce! These magnificent trees thrive in the misty rain forests, creating the magical green canopies draped with moss.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: The Hoh Rain Forest in Olympic National Park receives 140-170 inches of rain per year, making it one of the wettest places in the continental United States. This abundance of moisture creates an enchanted world of green.
